1.3.4.1.intro: Inventory is one of the most significant assets for manufacturing, trading, and distribution businesses. Accurate stock records are essential for financial reporting, operational efficiency, and obtaining working capital finance. A Stock Audit helps verify the existence, quantity, valuation, and management of inventory while identifying discrepancies that may affect business performance.

1.3.4.1.introRest: At Ritesh Arora & Associates, we provide independent Stock Audit services for businesses across various industries, helping management and lenders obtain assurance over inventory records and valuation.
1.3.4.1.body:
Our Stock Audit Services Include

Physical Verification of Inventory

We conduct verification of inventory to confirm its existence and accuracy.

Our audit includes:

  1. Physical stock verification.
  2. Quantity reconciliation.
  3. Identification of shortages and excess stock.
  4. Verification of inventory records.

Inventory Valuation Review

We examine inventory valuation methods to ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards.

Our review includes:

  1. Valuation methodology assessment.
  2. Verification of obsolete and slow-moving inventory.
  3. Cost allocation review.
  4. Inventory provisioning assessment.

Inventory Reconciliation

We reconcile physical stock with accounting records and inventory management systems.

Our services include:

  1. Stock register reconciliation.
  2. Financial record verification.
  3. Inventory movement analysis.
  4. Investigation of discrepancies.

Audit Reporting

We provide a detailed report highlighting observations, discrepancies, and recommendations for improving inventory management.

Benefits of Stock Audit

  1. Accurate inventory records.
  2. Improved stock control.
  3. Reliable inventory valuation.
  4. Better financial reporting.
  5. Reduced inventory losses.
  6. Enhanced lender confidence.

Reliable Inventory Verification Services

Our Stock Audit services help businesses maintain accurate inventory records, strengthen stock management practices, and improve the reliability of financial reporting.
